texto: When an adjective is placed in front of the noun he describes, he receives almost always the «-e»: «de nieuwe fiets» (the new bike), «de grote tafel» (the big table) disinence. The only important exception occurs when the noun is neutral (het-woord) and is accompanied by the undetermined article «een» (or without article): «een nieuw boek» (a new book), «een klein huis» (a small house), where the adjective is left without -e.

frases.nl: Nee, mijn fiets is klein en oud.
frases.es: No, mi bicicleta es pequeña y vieja.
frases.en: No, my bike is small and old.

frases.nl: Die grote fiets is van mijn broer.
frases.es: Esa bicicleta grande es de mi hermano.
frases.en: That big bike is my brother's.

frases.nl: Dan neem ik het kleine boek mee.
frases.es: Entonces me llevo el libro pequeño.
frases.en: Then I'll take the little book.

bloques.pregunta: Why do you say «de nieuwe fiets» but «een nieuw boek»?

opciones.texto: Because «boek» is neutral and with «een» the adjective does not add -e, while with «de» it always adds -e
opciones.explicacion: It is the adtributive flexion rule for het words with indefinite article.

opciones.texto: Porque «fiets» es plural y «boek» es singular
Because «nieuw» is an irregular adjective that only changes with transport
opciones.explicacion: The rule depends on the gender of the noun and the determinant, not the meaning.

opciones.explicacion: In predictive position after «is» the adjectives go without bending: «klein en oud».
The -e termination is only added when the adjective directly precedes the noun.

opciones.explicacion: With the particular article «het», the adjective adjective does receive the -e («het kleine boek») termination.
The -e would only be omitted if it carried «een» («een klein boek»), not «het».
